title: Numbers 8:23–26
context: A short rule sets the Levites’ years of service: from twenty-five years old they enter the work of the Tent of Meeting, and at fifty they stop the heavy work but may still assist their brothers in their duties. (Numbers 4 counts Levites from thirty to fifty for the carrying work; interpreters explain the difference in several ways.) The passage closes the Levites’ consecration with ordered, lifelong service.

verses.text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD speaks to Moses again, now about the Levites’ term of service. Arminian readers note God’s practical care. Both traditions agree that the final instruction sets the boundaries of the Levites’ working life.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s ordering of even the length of service, so that ministry has a beginning and an end. Shared ground: God’s word regulates the Levites’ ministry from beginning to end.

verses.text: “This is what is assigned to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward they shall go in to wait on the service in the work of the Tent of Meeting;
verses.arminianNotes: Levites begin service at twenty-five. Numbers 4:3 gives thirty for the carrying work, and interpreters explain the difference variously, for example as a training period or as differing tasks. Arminian readers see preparation for service. Both traditions avoid overconfident harmonization.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers acknowledge the difference with Numbers 4 and note that the text does not explain it. Shared ground: God sets the age for service, and the Levites enter their work in an orderly way.

verses.text: and from the age of fifty years they shall retire from doing the work, and shall serve no more,
verses.arminianNotes: At fifty the Levites retire from the heavy work of the Tent of Meeting. Arminian readers see God’s care for aging servants. Both traditions agree that the rule recognizes physical limits and protects the work itself.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s wisdom in setting limits on service, so that strength is matched to the demands of the task. Shared ground: God cares for those who serve, and the rule protects both the Levites and the work.

verses.text: but shall assist their brothers in the Tent of Meeting, to perform the duty, and shall perform no service. This is how you shall have the Levites do their duties.”
verses.arminianNotes: Retired Levites may assist their brothers but do no heavy service. Arminian readers see a continuing role for older servants. Both traditions agree that experience remains valuable even when strength declines.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the provision as honoring older Levites while protecting the work. Shared ground: there is a place for every stage of life in God’s service, and the chapter closes with ordered ministry.
